feat.name: Milkification
entries: You not only digest your prey, you are able to turn them into delicious milk, cum, or other liquid for others to consume! (this feat will use milk for its description, but is usable for any sort of liquid.

items: When you digest a meal, instead of gaining the normal benefits from digestion, you can instead turn them into milk. You gain an amount of milk equal to the bulk of all your digested food/prey in capacity points.

As an action, you can feed any number of capacity points worth of milk to an adjacent {@condition willing|lustvore} creature, or an unwilling one if they are {@condition grappled}. This milk heals 1 hit point per capacity, and is considered food as well.

As an attack, you may expend 1 or more points of milk up to your level to fire off a milk shot. This deals {@dice 1d6} + milk points of lewd damage, and the target must make a DC 10 + expended milk points Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they are coated with milk. While coated, they are in difficult terrain and have disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws. A creature may use its action to wipe off the milk.

feat.name: Miniature Meatarian
entries: The smallest of the small, your hunger rivals that of predators thrice your size, as do your curves. Many predators have seen you as nothing more than a bite sized snack, only to find themselves made yours! You gain the following:

items: You are considered one size larger for the purposes of Capacity and Predator size.
You suffer no penalty to grappling against prey two sizes or more larger than yourself.

feat.name: Multiple Arms
entries: Generally, folks with multiple arms have a set of 4 arms total, but some may have even more than that. You gain the following effects:

items: You now have 2 additional arms and hands. These extra arms can manipulate an object, open or close a door or container, pick up or set down an object, or wield one weapon that has the light property in each.

You now can do an unarmed attack or lewd strike as a bonus action, but you do not gain your ability modifier to damage, unless that modifier is negative. You gain the ability modifier to damage if you gain the {@optfeature two-weapon fighting} style. The damage dice size for this bonus action unarmed attack stays at {@dice 1d4} no matter what other features say.

feat.name: Ogre's Belch
entries: Your belches are as powerful as an ogre's, bellowing out humid gusts of air that disrupt your enemies. As a bonus action, you can do one of the following:

items: You belch out a gust of powerful air. This is treated as a {@action shove}, except you can do it at a target up to 10 feet away.

You belch out a humid musky cloud. Choose a creature within 10 feet that you can see. They must make a Constitution saving throw DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Constitution modifier or be {@condition poisoned} until the end of their next turn.

Your belch sends an object inside of you flying, such as the bones of your digested meals. Make a ranged attack with 20/40 range that you are proficient in. On a hit, this attack deals {@dice 1d4} + Dexterity modifier bludgeoning, piercing, slashing, OR lewd damage depending on the nature of the object. When uncertain, ask your DM.

Your belch is a splitting cry, deafening those around you. All creatures within 10 feet must make a Constitution saving throw DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Constitution modifier or be {@condition deafened} until the end of your next turn.

feat.name: Predatory Confidence
entries: You are more than simply a predator, you are an alpha. One look from your steely gaze is all it takes to let anyone know you are not to be trifled with. Or perhaps, one look is all it takes to instill submission. You gain the following effects:

items: You gain proficiency in either {@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}. If you are already proficient, you gain expertise in your chosen skill.

After swallowing a prey during your turn, as a free action you can extend out your predatory aura, letting all your potential prey know of their lovely or terrifying fate. Pick either frightening, or charming. All creatures of your choice within 15 feet must then make a Wisdom saving throw equal to 8 + your Charisma modifier + proficiency mod. On a failure, they are either {@condition frightened} or {@condition charmed} towards you for one minute depending on which aura you picked. At the end of its turn, an affected creature may make another save to shake off this effect. If they are {@condition charmed}, they are awestruck by your allure and may not move away from you, and may roll the test again if you or your allies do anything harmful to them, including {@condition devouring|lustvore}. You can use this ability once per short or long rest.

feat.name: Predatory Occupant
entries: You are not only used to being inside a belly, you know how to turn it to your predatory advantage, turning it into a symbiotic relationship. After all, with only one way in, all you need to do is open your mouth and wait.. You gain the following effects:

items: While {@condition swallowed|lustvore}, if another creature is fully {@condition swallowed|lustvore} into your same orifice, you may initiate a devour check as a reaction with advantage. On a success, you are able to gulp them down instantly. On a failure the prey manages to squirm their way away and is deposited into the stomach normally.

When you digest a meal, your predator gains the same effect for the digested meal. If you and your host predator have a separate capacity, calculate the digested meals capacity against the predator's capacity rather than your own for the predator's digestion benefits.

feat.name: Regurgitator
entries: You are quite accustomed to spitting out creatures and objects within your body, sometimes with devastating effect. You gain the following abilities:

items: You may now regurgitate creatures and objects as a bonus action, rather than an action.

In place of an attack, you may spit out a tiny size object or creature that was inside you. This is considered a ranged attack, has a range of 30/120, and deals {@dice 1d10} + Dexterity modifier damage. This damage is either bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing depending on the object. If this was a creature, on a hit the creature takes the same damage as the target.

feat.name: Semen Demon
entries: In olden lore, vampires were charming creatures that were known to lull their victims into a false sense of security and drink their blood. Though, there exists a breed of vampires that feed on more sensual fluids. You gain the following abilities:

items: When you suck on a {@condition charmed} or friendly creature, you can drain them over the course of one minute. You can gain 1 capacity point of sexual fluids and restore {@dice 1d6} + Charisma modifier hit points. You can do this up to half a creature's base bulk before you drain them completely, and cannot use this feature against them again until after their next long rest.

When you take the {@action grapple} or {@action devour|lustvore} action and it succeeds, you may declare to suck on the target's genitals as a bonus action. When you do, they take {@dice 1d6} + Charisma modifier in Lewd damage. You heal by half of the damage dealt. If they are reduced to 0 hit points by this, they are considered drained and gain a level of {@condition exhaustion}. They are also {@condition charmed} by you as they regard you with a lustful afterglow and are {@condition willing|lustvore} to be devoured (although not digested!)

feat.name: Sensational Touch
entries: Through your tongue, your body, your curves, or a breath, you are able to stun your opponents into sensual submission. You gain the following ability:

items: While grappling or in a devour contest with a creature (or one held in an otherwise compromising position where you can get at them with it), you can spend your action to force the target to make a Wisdom saving throw vs 8 + Charisma or Dexterity modifier + Proficiency Bonus or be overwhelmed with pleasure for 1 minute. During this effect, the 'victim' is {@condition charmed}. They regard you lustfully. This charm breaks if you or your companions do any non-lewd damage to the target or their allies, and they may roll the saving throw again whenever you deal lewd damage to the target.

If you spend 1 minute physically touching and physically flirting with someone, you can make a Charisma({@skill Performance}) check contested by the creature's Wisdom({@skill Insight}) check. If you or your companions are fighting the creature, your check automatically fails. If your check succeeds, the target is {@condition charmed} by you as long as it remains within 10 feet of you and for 1 minute thereafter, as they now regard you with sexual infatuation. This charm breaks if you or your companions take any hostile actions or deal damage to them or their companions.

feat.name: Shortstack Predator
entries: Although smaller than most, you are just as hungry as the biggest of them, and this shows in your voracious appetite and enhanced curves. You gain the following effects:

items: You are considered one size larger for the purposes of your capacity and devour checks where you are a predator.
Your bulk is increased by one size larger.
Whenever you attempt to devour a creature of a larger size than you, you may choose to gain advantage on the roll. You may use this ability once per short rest.

prerequisite.other: Small or tiny size, does not work if effectively permanently enlarged or similar.

feat.name: Silent Prey
entries: You have mastered an art of infiltrating predators and going unnoticed inside them to an inhuman degree.

items: For purposes of {@condition devouring|lustvore} or being devoured, you may choose to count as one size smaller whenever it benefits you.

When you are hidden from a creature you may attempt to crawl inside of them without their notice. As an action, you may attempt to force your way inside another creature of equal or larger size. If they are unwilling, roll an {@skill Athletics} or {@skill Acrobatics} contest vs their {@skill Athletics} or {@skill Acrobatics}. If you fail, your stealth is broken. If you succeed, you enter a devour contest with 1 success against the creature where you must achieve a number of successes equal to what a creature of their size would need to devour you. If they achieve a number of successes equal to yours then you fail the devour contest and your stealth is broken.

When feeding yourself to another, if you are more than 1 size smaller than the predator, you receive a +1 for each size category beyond that point. (If a tiny creature is slipping into a medium creature, they get a +1. Tiny into a large is a +2, etc)
A predator that is unaware of you cannot begin to digest you until they either eat something/someone else or you indicate your presence to them.
If you create noise or produce a bulge inside your predator, any observing creature has disadvantage to notice.

feat.name: Skull-collector
entries: Rather than keep the souls of your devoured prey in your body, you've instead learned to tie them to their skulls. You gain the following effects:

items: When you fully digest prey, you may belch up their skull whenever you choose. This skull acts as a magical object, and is possessed by the soul of the prey it belonged to.
The prey is bound to the skull until it is broken and is able to speak freely but cannot move.
There is no limit to how many skulls you can create and have active at a given time, unlike normal soul vore.

feat.name: Small
entries: Due to some quirk of heritage or of a magical nature, your body is unusually small for your race. Oftentimes, this turns you into a shortstack!

items: You permanently reduce your size down by one or more steps, up to a maximum size decrease of small, and you gain 10 feet to their walking speed up to a maximum of 40 feet including racial bonuses. Other effects can stack on top of this after like feats or class bonuses.
You gain one additional vore or lewd feat upon taking this feat.
Your decreased size may draw unwanted attention.

prerequisite.other: Medium or Larger size, Incompatible with the Large feat.

feat.name: Smotherer
entries: You are adept at using your body to smother your prey when you grapple.
As a bonus action, you can smother a creature you are grappling. The target is {@condition blinded} for as long as they remain {@condition grappled}.

feat.name: Soothing Stomach
entries: Your belly carries fortifying properties and can serve as a comfortable resting spot for the weary. You gain the following benefits:

items: When a creature completes a long rest spent entirely within your stomach, they gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Constitution modifier. In addition, they regain all expended hit dice, and remove up to 3 levels of {@condition exhaustion}.
When a creature completes a short rest spent entirely within your body, they gain max rolls on hit dice spent for healing.
Any healing spells or effects (excluding hit dice) effecting prey inside your belly regain additional hit points equal to your Constitution modifier

feat.name: Soul Absorption
entries: You are able to trap your prey's soul and essence inside your body, and may reform them at a later time or simply torment them as part of your body fat. You gain the following abilities:

items: Upon fully absorbing a creature, you may declare to Soul Absorb them. In doing so you gain all the normal benefits of digestion. However, their soul is now trapped as part of your body. This must be marked in some physical and visible way upon your body. This could be a tattoo of them, tallymarks, tribal tattoo markings that cover more of your body the more prey there are, etc.

Soul absorbed prey cannot take any actions, speak, or do anything that might indicate their presence. However, they do retain their sentience, and generally feel whatever part of the body they have been ‘absorbed' into. Soul absorbed prey can telepathically communicate with other absorbed targets and you, if you allow them to.

You can reform any prey you have chosen to soul absorb. Upon consuming a meal of equal or greater capacity size to the original size of your soul absorbed prey, you can choose to reform one or more soul absorbed creatures during a long rest, with the total capacity of creatures reformed being under the total capacity of the meal. Upon being reformed, they are nude and have no equipment, and suffer 1 level of {@condition exhaustion}.

You can keep a number of soul absorbed prey equal to your Charisma modifier + your level. Should you ever exceed that amount, you must either release an absorbed creature's soul, or permanently absorb them. Upon permanent absorption you are no longer able to speak with them as their essence gradually and blissfully becomes one with yours. A creature absorbed this way cannot be revived through normal means except through exceptionally powerful magic such as wishes.

Should you ever die, your non-permanently absorbed targets souls are released. If you are reformed, they can willingly choose to return to your body. All permanently absorbed creatures always return, as they are part of you now.

During a long rest, you can focus your attention upon one of your soul absorbed prey and gain proficiency in one skill they are proficient in. You may gain one skill proficiency this way but can replace this with another long rest. You lose this benefit if they are ever reformed.

When you would be fully absorbed by a creature, you may optionally allow them to declare you as Soul Absorbed instead, following the above rules as long as they are {@condition willing|lustvore}. This only functions for you, and does not grant them the feat.

feat.name: Speedy Reformer
entries: Your body is able to more easily reform than most people, giving you the following bonuses:

items: Anytime you would be reformed from a long rest after having died by digestion, you may instead reform on a short rest.
Anytime an ability would require a meal of equal size, they instead require a meal of ½ your size to reform you.

Anytime an ability only allows reformation or revival within a certain time limit, that time is extended a number of months equal to your Charisma modifier. If this time limit is less than the one of the spell/effect, the time limit is unaffected.

feat.name: Stomach of Holding
entries: Perhaps due to a magical experiment, or simply your body adapting to your desires, you have somehow gained a second stomach pouch.

items: You gain a new space in your body known as your stomach of holding. When you swallow a creature or at the end of your turn before you deal digestion damage, you can push an object or a creature from your stomach into your stomach of holding. You can hold up to 500lbs. of inanimate objects or 8 capacity worth of creatures in your stomach of holding without counting towards your Capacity.
If you ever exceed your capacity, the heaviest object or creature in your stomach of holding is pushed into your normal stomach.
As a bonus action, you can pull any object out of your stomach of holding by regurgitating it (or pushing it out through another orifice!).

Regardless of what is in your stomach of holding, you may choose to appear as if you have nothing in your stomach, and it is impossible for people to detect anything you have inside your stomach of holding outside of extraordinary magical means that would allow them to see inside normal bags of holding.

feat.name: Stomach Squatter
entries: Some creatures have taken their love for residing in bellies to an extreme: They don't merely enjoy bellies, they practically live in them, and will fight any attempt to remove them from their comfortable home!

items: When you take a long rest inside a belly, you regain all of your hit dice rather than half.

Once per short rest, as an action you may choose to make yourself near impossible to digest. You gain immunity to all non-psychic digestion damage, so long as you do not take any type of actions/bonus actions/reactions. This state lasts until you take an action/bonus action/reaction. You may not rest in this state, nor gain benefits from rest.

When a predator attempts to regurgitate you and you do not wish to be spit out, they must roll a Constitution saving throw vs 8 + your Dexterity or Strength modifier + your Proficiency Bonus. On a failure, you remain in their belly. If they fail on their saving throw by 5 or more, they cannot attempt again for another 1 hour or until damaged by you as you wedge yourself deeper inside of them. These effects do not stop them from digesting you!

feat.name: Struggler
entries: You are an exceptionally strong struggler, and able to kick and punch in ways to make your predator more than uncomfortable. While inside a creature, you do not have disadvantage on skill checks. In addition, when you successfully take the struggle action, you may choose one additional effect from the following:

items: The next attack against the predator is made with advantage.
The next saving throw the predator rolls is made with a disadvantage until your next turn.
The next ability check the predator rolls is made with a disadvantage until your next turn.
The predator takes damage equal to {@dice 1d10} + your Strength modifier
The predator must make a {@status concentration} check at DC 8 + Strength modifier + Proficency Bonus. On a failure, they are poisoned until your next turn.

feat.name: Slick With Spit
entries: Your salivary glands work on overdrive. You gain the following effects:

items: Your spit is now exceptionally potent. You gain a new feature, spit, which is used by various abilities. While a creature is affected by your spit, all devour checks against them have advantage and all grapple tests against them have disadvantage.

Whenever a prey escapes from a devour contest where you had at least 1 success, or is otherwise regurgitated from being fully {@condition swallowed|lustvore} by you, they are covered in copious amounts of slick saliva or other juices for 1 minute. During this time they are affected by your spit, and at the end of their turn they must roll a Dexterity saving throw vs DC 8 + Constitution modifier + Proficency Bonus or your spell save DC, whichever is higher, or fall prone. They can use their action to wipe off the spit.

As an action, you can huck a spitball at a creature you can see within 30 feet. They must make a Dexterity saving throw vs DC 8 + Constitution modifier + Proficency Bonus or your spell save DC, whichever is higher, or be affected by your spit for 1 minute. They can use their action to wipe off the spit.

While you are grappling or {@condition devouring|lustvore} a creature, you may attempt to lick them as a bonus action. They must roll a Dexterity saving throw vs DC 8 + Constitution modifier + Proficency Bonus or your spell save DC, whichever is higher, or be affected by your spit until the end of your turn.

feat.name: Slow Digestion
entries: Your system is quite patient and slow at breaking down its prey. However, this makes it quite efficient. You gain the following effects:

items: Your digestion lasts 4 times as long as it normally would for a meal. While digesting, at least 1 capacity worth of creature, you do not require food or water. In addition, most prey generally last for many hours before fully expiring. When you put prey into the “digested” state to start processing, they hold on for 1/2 of your digestion time before technically expiring. During this time, should you be forced to regurgitate your prey, they will exit in a stable state.

Every long rest you take while you are digesting at least ½ your capacity, you restore all your hit dice rather than half, and you gain your Constitution modifier + your level of temporary hit points upon waking up.

feat.name: Swift Digestion
entries: Your system is fast at mushing and sucking up your prey when you can take the time to let your gut work. You gain the following effects:

items: So long as you are equal to or below capacity, you can finish digestion on a short rest.
If you are above capacity but not over your max capacity, digestion can be finished on a long rest.
Your time for digesting a max capacity meal is halved.

feat.name: Symbiotic Predator
entries: Your belly has learned to treat its prey as more than just a quick meal, instead gradually sapping nutrients while simultaneously curing their own hunger through a unique relationship.

items: While inside your body, your prey never needs to eat or drink.

You may choose to make any number of creatures inside you immune to your digestion as a free action, and may retract it just as easily. Gear does not count as part of a creature (and thus may be digested separately).
While you are filled with at least ½ your capacity's worth of living creatures, you are considered fed.

Once per short or long rest, when you have at least one creature inside of you, you can draw upon your prey for a surge of temporary strength as a free action. Doing so allows you to reroll any one attack roll or skill check during your turn.

feat.name: Symbiotic Prey
entries: You have a unique relationship with your predators, and are able to provide them with sustenance and keep yourself sustained for far longer than normal. While inside a creature, you gain the following effects:

items: The creature you are inside never needs to eat or drink.
While you are inside a creature, you don't need to eat or drink.
If you are inside a predator that is {@condition willing|lustvore} to allow it, you can make yourself immune to their digestion as a free action.

As a bonus action you can heal your predator's hit points for {@dice 1d10} + your Charisma modifier. This improves to ({@dice 2d10}) at 5th level, ({@dice 3d10}) at 10th level, ({@dice 4d10}) at 15th level, and ({@dice 5d10}) at 20th level. You may use this ability once per short rest.

feat.name: Tail Vore
entries: You have learned how to use your tail as an extension of your drive to consume. You gain the following effects:

items: If it did not already, your tail now counts as another orifice you can use to devour targets, and can be used as another hand for grappling.

As a bonus action, when your tail is not already {@condition devouring|lustvore} something, you can attempt to devour creatures with your tail even if they are not {@condition grappled}. This test is done with disadvantage if they are not {@condition grappled}, or normally if they are {@condition grappled}.

feat.name: Transformative Digestion
entries: You have learned how to successfully assimilate souls you devour into parts of your body directly. You gain the following effects:

items: After soul absorbing a creature, friend or foe, you may attempt to transform them into a part of yourself. Whichever part they become, they will have a somewhat 50/50 control over that part of you, and remain sentient and keep most of their intelligence.
When you release the creature's soul, the part returns to normal.

The creature added to you can only perform actions relative to its new position; a cock may be able to vore targets, while a tail might help you grapple or bludgeon enemies- likewise, someone added as simple fat can't do more than wobble.

After being Soul Absorbed by a creature, you may allow them to transform you into a part of themself following the above rules as long as they are {@condition willing|lustvore}. This only functions for you, and does not grant them the feat.

feat.name: Tough Gut
entries: Your gut might as well be lined with iron for how tough it is. You gain the following effects:

items: You gain resistance to all slashing, bludgeoning, and piercing damage done inside you.
You may use your reaction to gain advantage against any prey attempting to struggle.
You are immune to all negative effects of potions, poisons, food, and other digested materials.

feat.name: Voracious
entries: A skilled predator is quick in their consumption.
As a bonus action, you may make a {@action devour|lustvore} attack in the same turn you make a {@action grapple} attack.

Where there is civilization, there are almost certainly golems. Being tireless creations that require no food, sustenance, or rest, golems are often treated as a premium workforce. Where a man can do a job well, a golem can do it perfectly and consistently.

However, despite their usefulness, they come at an inherent risk. Over time, Golems inevitably begin to develop their own personalities, traits, desires, quirks, and even free will. In most cases, this is not a problem, and in fact rather a pleasant surprise. After all, due to their usually helpful nature, Golems naturally desire to assist where they can, and often become true members of the families and households they serve. However, this is not always the case, and sometimes it is difficult to spot until it's too late. The golemancers who often manage and repair them are often too biased towards their own creations to be used as good judges of character, and more than one golem has realized the individuals they serve are not worthy of their services, and begin to slowly twist and bend their commands to serve their own purposes…
{@b Golems and Adventurers:}

Free Golems are exceedingly rare in the world. More than once free golems have gone on murderous rampages against their former masters, or most terrifyingly, simply had no concept of why their actions were wrong at all. Thus, most that become free are often slain due to their logically warped consciousnesses. However, those golems that begin to learn and understand the world often desire to gather more data and experience “life” outside of their normal functions, and often choose to integrate with wandering parties and adventurers.

entries.name: Age
entries: Golems are constructed and animated, and do not age.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Golems always are created lawful, as they obey their runic bindings to a fault. However, golems often slowly begin to develop quirks, a personality, and free will in the constraints of their bindings. Or in some rare cases of freed golems, complete free will. In the course of time, they may develop a wide variety of alignments.

entries.name: Size
entries: Golems are usually made in a similar image to their creators, and are usually between 5-6ft and medium size. However golems can be made of any size.

entries.name: Half-Construct
entries: You were created to have remarkable fortitude, represented by the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition poisoned}, and you have resistance to poison damage.
You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe.
You are immune to disease.
You don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep.

entries.name: Sentry's Rest
entries: When you take a long rest, you must spend at least six hours in an inactive, motionless state, rather than sleeping. In this state, you appear inert, but it doesn't render you {@condition unconscious}, and you can see and hear as normal.

entries.name: Hardy Construction
entries: Golems have a natural armor of 12 + Dexterity modifier.

entries.name: Languages
entries: A golem knows common and the language of its creator.

action.name: Devour
entries: When you want to swallow a creature, you can use the {@action Attack} action to make a Special melee Attack, a Devour. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, this Attack replaces one of them. A creature must be {@condition grappled}, {@condition restrained}, or otherwise unable to move or have a moment speed of 0 to target them with this attack.

You must make a Strength({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity({@skill Acrobatics}) check contested by the target's Strength({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity({@skill Acrobatics}) check (the target chooses the ability to use). The prey may choose to be {@condition willing|lustvore}and automatically fail this test. If you succeed, you and the target enter a Devour Contest, and you gain a single success on the devour contest.

{@i Note: Like the {@action Grapple} and {@action Shove} actions, you can replace only one of your attacks that are part of your attack action with devour attacks. If you have multiple attack actions (such as fighter's action surge) you can replace one attack with a devour on both attack actions.}
{@b Devour Action and incapacitated creatures}

The devour action assumes you are attempting to devour unwilling and conscious creatures. If the creature is unable or unwilling to resist, you do not need to grapple them first in order to start a devour contest. To specify when this is commonly applicable:

You do not need to grapple creatures that automatically fail ability checks, or strength and dexterity saving throws in order to start a devour contest. This includes but is not limited to: {@condition blinded}, {@condition unconscious}, {@condition paralyzed}, {@condition petrified}, and {@condition stunned}.

action.name: Force-Feed
entries: You may try to force-feed yourself to another creature. As an {@action Attack}, when you are {@condition grappled} or grappling a creature, or in devour contest against another creature with you as prey, you may attempt to force yourself into the creature.

If they are unwilling, they may roll to resist the devour contest as if they were predator. On a success or if they are {@condition willing|LustVore}, the predator gains one devour success against you.

action.name: Rub
entries: All creatures now have access to the following attack, Rub.

You may only target rub against a creature with at least one or more creature inside of it. This attack automatically hits one creature inside the target creature and deals lewd or bludgeoning damage equal to:

condition.name: Defeated
entries: These rules purposefully contain many options to non-lethally subdue a foe. A live squirming prey to gulp down is far more interesting than a dead or unconscious one after all! For this purpose, a new incapacitated state is added: {@i The {@condition defeated|lustvore} State}.

When a foe is brought to 0 hit points by a player character through any means (including lewd damage, range damage, spells, and so forth) instead of being unconscious or killed, they may instead be put into the {@i Defeated} state. {@condition defeated|lustvore} foes follow all the same rules as being unconscious: They are {@condition incapacitated}, it drops whatever its holding and falls {@condition prone}, it fails its Dexterity and Strength checks, all attacks vs it gain advantage, and attacks within 5 feet are critical hits.

However, {@condition defeated|lustvore} foes are still considered conscious. They cannot move in any significant amount, but they can weakly speak and struggle until they regain 1 hit point. If left alone, they may be able to crawl at a rate of 5 feet per turn at DM's discretion.

condition.name: Devouring
entries: Also colloquially referred to as the “nomming” condition, this condition simply means you are in the process of {@condition devouring|lustvore} someone through a devour contest or being devoured by someone else. So long as you remain in a devour contest either as predator or prey, you suffer the following effects from the devour contest condition:

items: You are {@condition restrained}, and {@condition grappled} if you are prey.
You are locked into a devour contest, either as predator or prey. Keep track of successes per the {@condition devouring|lustvore} rules for both pred and prey.
The {@i lewded} condition lasts until the end of your next turn, though at your and the DM's discretion may last longer.
A {@i lewded} creature automatically fails any contested roll against the source of their lewding.
A {@i lewded} creature has disadvantage to all checks, saves, and attack rolls made until the condition ends.

Once after combat (with DM permission), a character who was {@i Lewded} may recover up to a third of their health rounded down. This recovery can only be done once regardless of how many times the condition is triggered, and if it is not taken after the combat is over the potential recovery is lost. This is usually flavored as a rush of energy following an exciting situation, but may be flavored as you like.

condition.name: Swallowed
entries: When a predator succeeds on a devour contest vs a creature, that creature gains the new {@i Swallowed} condition.

items: You have disadvantage on all skill checks.
You are {@condition restrained}.
You have total cover from outside effects and cannot see outside of the creature and stomach you are within.
You automatically move where a predator does and are considered to be in the predator's same square, and adjacent for the purposes of ranged attacks.

You must successfully make a {@status concentration} check vs the predator's stomach AC before casting a spell. If you fail, you do not cast the spell, but you do not lose the spell slot or other resource.
If you are concentrating on a spell and the creature your {@condition swallowed|lustvore} by takes damage, you must make a {@status concentration} check at DC 10 or ½ the damage, whichever is higher.

condition.name: Willing
entries: In these rules, there are many spells and effects that refer to a creatures “willingness” to be devoured. If a creature is {@i willing}, it means they are perfectly ok with being devoured by select creatures, likely due to thinking of them as trusted allies or lovers, and may have the new {@i Willing} condition upon them.

Outside of effects that specify a creature's willingness (often as part of charm effects), it is always the creature's right to decide if they are {@i willing} or {@i unwilling}. Generally, all creatures are considered to be {@i unwilling}, unless otherwise specified by them or an ability, and thus all normal vore rules apply to them.. This is also done on a case by case basis. A creature can be {@condition willing|lustvore} to be devoured by one predator, but not another. A creature can, at any point as a free action on or outside of their turn, declare if they are {@condition willing|lustvore} or not {@condition willing|lustvore} to be devoured by another creature.
The {@i willing} condition has the following effects:

items: A predator no longer needs to grapple you in order to initiate a {@condition devouring|LustVore|devour contest}.
You are considered to auto-fail all {@condition devouring|LustVore|devour contest} checks

entries: {@b A note on {@condition willing|lustvore} condition and being {@condition charmed}:}

Being {@condition charmed} in relation to vore is a difficult thing to determine. There are many factors to consider, such as how the world views vore, how dangerous it is, and so forth. These rules should be adapted depending on the universal context. However in general, charms should be considered as follows:

Charm effects generally cause creatures to act as a friendly acquaintance, or a trusted friend. As such, due to the often dangers of vore, most {@condition charmed} creatures will still resist being eaten, and consider being devoured as a hostile action on par with someone attempting to strike them with a sword.
Due to this, {@condition charmed} creatures are never {@condition willing|lustvore} targets unless directly specified by the spell or effect. The GM can overrule this when it makes sense.

Thus when a creature does not consider {@condition devouring|lustvore} as a hostile action due to an effect but is not a {@condition willing|lustvore} target, they may still resist being eaten. If a predator continues trying to devour an unwilling target, the GM may rule that it breaks the effect of the charm as it suddenly becomes a hostile action.

spell.name: Absorb Power
entries: Choose one creature inside of you. They must roll a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they take {@damage 3d6} force damage or half as much on a success, and you gain an equal amount of bonus damage to your next melee, ranged, or spell damage roll within the next minute. If this is an attack that affects multiple targets, you only add the bonus damage to the first target damaged.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each slot level above 4th.

spell.name: Acidify
entries: You touch a predator with creatures in their stomach, filling their belly with acid. All living creatures in the stomach must take a Constitution saving throw or suffer {@damage 4d10} acid damage or half as much on a success.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d10} for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Amplify Acids
entries: The target creature's gastric acids magically intensify, quickly melting any devoured creatures to sludge. For the duration of the spell, the target creature's digestion deals an additional {@damage 2d8} damage, and they digest meals in half the time.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a 5th level spell slot, the damage increases to {@dice 3d8}. When you cast this spell using a 7th level spell slot, the damage increases to {@dice 4d8}.

spell.name: Anti-Acid Shell
entries: You briefly turn your skin into a smooth, digestion resistant shell, gaining resistance to all non-magical digestion damage, and all acid damage for one minute.

spell.name: Arcane Digestion
entries: Choose one damage type between acid, fire, lightning, cold, or thunder. For the duration of this spell, your digestion deals that type of magical damage, and gains an additional {@damage 1d6} damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each slot level above 1st.

spell.name: Arcane Jaws
entries: Your maw (or body part) is imbued with magical ravenous energy, stretching to attempt to swallow your unfortunate prey! You make a melee spellcasting attack roll against your target. On a success, you deal {@damage 1d4} force damage, you are considered to have started a devour contest against the creature with one success.
You may continue this devour contest on subsequent turns, and can use your spellcasting ability modifier in place of your strength or dexterity score for the checks in this contest.
{@b Cantrip Upgrade.} This damage increases by {@dice 1d4} when you reach 5th level ({@damage 2d4}), 11th level ({@damage 3d4}), and 17th level ({@damage 4d4}).

spell.name: Arcane Leash
entries: A bright cord of energy whips between two targets, binding them together. Target must make a Dexterity saving throw to avoid being tethered. Once tethered, the target may make a Strength saving throw as an action to break the leash.

Once leashed, the two targets cannot move away from each other. The creature that has higher bulk can drag the other creature with them if they move; if both creatures have the same bulk, it results in either one being able to drag, but with only half your movement speed. When casting, you can opt to make one of the two targets yourself.

When leashed, any target (including yourself) has disadvantage on all devour checks to resist being eaten or {@condition swallowed|LustVore} by a predator swallowing the leash. Anyone who can grab the leash can make a contested Strength check as a bonus action to try to pull the leashed target towards themselves up to 30 feett per pull.

spell.name: Arousing Touch

components.m: a weapon with which you have proficiency and that is worth 1+ CP

entries: You brandish the weapon used in the spell's casting and make a melee attack with it against one creature within 5 feet of you. On a hit, the target suffers the attack's normal effects. If the attack deals damage, it can be Lewd damage or the weapon's normal damage type (your choice). Creatures hit by this attack receive a {@dice 1d4} penalty on their next saving throw made before the end of your next turn.

{@b Cantrip Upgrade.} Whether you deal Lewd damage or the weapon's normal damage type, the attack deals extra Lewd damage when you reach 5th level ({@damage 1d6}), 11th level ({@damage 2d6}), and 17th level ({@damage 3d6}).

spell.name: Aura of Lust
entries: An unnatural haze of magical pheromonal lust surrounds the caster for one minute, so strong that it blocks out all thoughts but those of sexual congress. Creatures who start their turn or move into the area within 10 feet of you must roll a Wisdom saving throw (max one test per turn). Failure means they are considered {@condition charmed} by you, and submit to their lustful desires, and immediately look for someone or something to fulfill their desires. A creature affected this way can do nothing but lewd actions and attacks. If two or more people are affected by the aura, they will look to satisfy their desires upon each other.

Creatures affected may roll another Wisdom saving throw to break out of the spell if they start their turn farther than 10 feet from you, upon taking non-lewd damage, or being subject to some potentially dangerous action (such as being eaten)

spell.name: Belch
entries: You release a tremorous wave of air, capable of knocking a creature off balance with sheer force. A creature within range that you can see must make a Strength saving throw. Upon a failure, they take {@damage 1d8} thunder damage and your next attack made against the creature is made with advantage until the end of your next turn. The damage becomes {@dice 1d10} if you currently have prey inside your stomach.

{@b Cantrip Upgrade.} This damage increases by {@dice 1d8} (or {@dice 1d10}) when you reach 5th level ({@damage 2d8} (or {@dice 2d10})), 11th level ({@damage 3d8} (or {@dice 3d10})), and 17th level ({@damage 4d8} (or {@dice 4d10})).

spell.name: Belly Fortune Telling
entries: While you are inside a belly, you can look into the gurgling acids surrounding you to see a portent of the future. You can ask one question to your deity or your divine proxy.

You are provided with a vision of your predator in relation to your question, always shown with the enhanced curves they would look like after digesting you. This vision portrays a scene relating to your question.

For example if you asked {@i “What is the greatest danger today?”}, you might receive a vision of your predator with busty curves fighting off an unknown ambush in the city streets. Or if your predator is untrustworthy, it might simply be a vision of them rubbing their chubby and digesting gut.

If you ask a question that cannot possibly relate to your predator, you receive nothing but gurgles. If you ask something that's too unclear, you might simply receive a vision of your predator with enhanced curves.

spell.name: Bellyport
entries: Target a creature you can see in range of the spell, and one creature to be the recipient. The target, and the recipient (if they are unwilling) must make a Wisdom saving throw as a bright flash of light erupts around them. On a failure, the target creature is teleported directly into the stomach of the recipient.

spell.name: Bellyport Ally
entries: Sometimes the best way to save someone is to put them inside your own belly, or that of an ally. You can pluck one {@condition willing|LustVore} ally (including yourself) you can see or otherwise know the exact location of from a troublesome location and materialize them fully {@condition swallowed|LustVore} inside your own body, or that of an ally within 120 feet. If your ally is already inside an enemy's stomach, the enemy creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw as an aura of bright light surrounds their belly. Should they succeed on their saving throw, the spell fails.

spell.name: Bodypouch
entries: Upon casting, choose one object you can hold in your hands. Your skin becomes malleable to that object and allows you to slip that object anywhere into your body as if your skin was water, making it nearly impossible to spot. For the duration of the spell, you are able to secretly draw and store the object on your body as a bonus action.

spell.name: Bottomless Hunger
entries: Touch a {@condition willing|LustVore} creature. For the duration of the spell, that creature has an unlimited capacity, is considered to be two sizes larger for the purposes of devour checks, and may devour creatures without grappling them first.

spell.name: Come to Me
entries: Choose a creature whom you know their face and name, that's also on the same plane of existence. The creature hears your voice and knows it's you summoning them. Provided they are {@condition willing|LustVore}, they are then instantly teleported to you (or inside you!).

If the creature is inside another creature, the enemy creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw as an aura of bright light surrounds their belly. Should they succeed on their saving throw, the spell fails.

This spell only works if both you and the target are in a location that allows for it. For example, this spell cannot be cast if you or the target are in an antimagic field, are in a special area that does not allow for dimensional teleportation, etc.

spell.name: Compress
entries: You touch one creature with at least one creature inside of them. For the duration of the spell, their body compresses itself until it appears that they have no creatures inside of them.

The target still suffers the normal effects of capacity penalties. In addition, particularly astute eyes can spot the slight bulges and unnatural look of the belly with an active DC 25 {@skill Perception} check.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 4th.

spell.name: Cursed Orgasm

components.m: a drop of sexual fluid mixed with a drop of weak acid

entries: You weave a magical pleasurable curse upon your target. The next time that the subject achieves orgasm, they are wracked with mind-breaking pleasure that causes {@damage 12d6} lewd damage. If this brings them to 0 hit points or lower, they are knocked {@condition unconscious} for {@dice 2d4} hours rather than {@condition defeated|LustVore}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 2d6} for each slot level above 3rd.

spell.name: Devouring Smite
entries: The next time you hit with a melee weapon attack or unarmed attack during this spell's duration, your attack deals an extra {@damage 1d6} force damage. Additionally, if the target is a creature, it must make a Strength saving throw. On a fail, you start a devour contest as if you had just successfully taken the devour action. Regardless of the result, the spell immediately ends.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Digestive Barrier
entries: Choose a creature within range that is just about to be {@condition swallowed|LustVore}. For the duration of this spell, the target is immune to non-magical digestion damage. You may also cast this spell on your turn as a bonus action.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell with a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the duration increases by 1 minute for every slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Dimensional Stomach
entries: Your touch alters a creature's stomach, turning it into its own demiplane. Touch a {@condition willing|LustVore} creature. For the duration, that creature's capacity is considered to be infinite.
Additionally, the creature is unburdened by the weight of their occupants, and their stomach appears as flat as when it is empty.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the duration increases by 8 hours for every spell slot above 6th level.

spell.name: Disrobe
entries: Choose a creature in range. The creature's clothing, including undergarments, belts, footwear, jewelry and other non-magical items not held, loosen and slide off as if covered in grease.

If the creature is wearing armor, they may make a Dexterity saving throw to keep their armor. Success indicates they manage to clutch their armor and keep it on. Failure means it too slides off, causing them to lose any armor AC bonus they may have.
Any items the creature is clutching or grasping , as well as magical items worn, do not slide off, and remain in their grasp and on their person.

It takes an action for a character to quickly re-don their clothing, and another action to re-don their armor. (a creature can re-don their armor without re-donning clothing first, although it might be quite uncomfortable!)

spell.name: Divine Mark
entries: You inscribe a personal magical mark upon another creature by touching their bare skin in some way, often through biting, a teasing flash of fingers, and so forth, and can potentially be done without the target's knowledge. This personal mark can take any form, but often is a hickey or some other possessive mark. This mark is visible unless covered up by clothing, makeup, etc.

For the duration of the spell, you always know the “rough” area that the target is in by knowing the direction they are from you, and a feeling of how close or near they are {@i (usually by one's loins or chest growing hotter the closer you are together)}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the mark lasts for an additional 24 hours for each slot level above the 1st.

spell.name: Elastify/Constrict
entries: You increase or decrease the elasticity and hunger of a predator. Choose one creature you can see within range. If the target is unwilling, it can make a Constitution saving throw. On a success, the spell has no effect.
{@i {@b Elastify}}. The predator counts as one size larger for the purpose of determining capacity.
{@i {@b Constrict}}. The predator counts as one size smaller for the purpose of determining capacity.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Elemental Fist
entries: Your fist overflows with elemental power. Choose an element between lightning, cold, fire, or acid, and make a melee spell attack roll against your target. On a hit, you deal {@damage 3d10} damage of your chosen element.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d10} for each slot level above 1st.

spell.name: Empower Body
entries: As an action, you infuse your body with magical strength. You gain 20 temporary hit points. Then you then choose one of the following effects to gain for the duration of the spell:
{@b {@i Power:}} Gain advantage on all Strength ability checks and saving throws, deal {@damage 1d6} extra damage on Strength based attacks
{@b {@i Grace:}} Gain advantage on all Dexterity ability checks and saving throws, deal {@damage 1d6} extra damage on Dexterity based attacks
{@b {@i Resilience:}} Gain advantage on all Constitution ability checks and saving throws, and gain an additional {@dice 4d6} temporary hit points.

spell.name: Enhance/Reduce Assets
entries: As an action, select a body part of a {@condition willing|LustVore} creature. That body part swells or reduces to a size of your choosing {@i (so long as it's not so large as to increase your size from Medium to Large and so forth!)}. This can be used to increase/decrease ass size, cock size, breast size, belly size, etc.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the duration becomes 24 hours. If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the duration becomes permanent.

spell.name: Entice
entries: You give one creature within range an irresistible scent. All predators within 30 feet of the creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. A target automatically succeeds on this saving throw if it can't be {@condition charmed}. On a failed save, the predators are affected by the spell, and must spend their turn attempting to consume the target creature. While under the effects of the spell, each affected predator has advantage on devour attacks made to {@action Devour} the target.

Whenever an affected creature takes damage, it gets to repeat the saving throw. When the target has been successfully {@condition swallowed|LustVore}, the predator who devoured the target becomes the new target of the spell, and all predators within 30 feet must pass the same Wisdom saving throw or repeat the process.

spell.name: Erotic Dance
entries: Your body's movements flow with magic sensuality, with your movements rippling across your target's body as if you were dancing against them.

Your target must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, they are {@condition charmed} until the end of your next turn, and you deal {@damage 3d8} lewd damage. On a success, they take half the damage and are not {@condition charmed}. If the target is adjacent, you can instead make a melee spellcasting attack roll.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each slot level above 1st.

spell.name: Favored Prey Protection
entries: You infuse a creature's guts to tell friend from foe. As part of this spell cast, you touch a creature. For the spell's duration, the chosen creature can make any number of creatures or objects inside of them immune to digestion damage as a bonus action, and may revoke the protection with another bonus action.

spell.name: Flavor/Disgust
entries: You point at a creature within range, altering its natural flavor.

{@i {@b Flavor}}. A creature of your choice within range must make a Dexterity saving throw or become irresistibly delicious to any predator. All creatures gain advantage on devour tests against the target, and predators may be tempted to consume them over other options.

{@i {@b Disgust}}. A creature of your choice within range becomes disgusting in flavor and scent to any predator. Whenever a predator attempts a devour check against them, they must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a fail, they cannot attempt to consume them, and waste their action or attack. On a success, they are immune to further disgust effects from this spell until its next rest.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you may select one additional target for each slot level above the 1st.

spell.name: Form Maw
entries: Touch a surface. Upon that surface, up to a 10 feet diameter circle, forms a magic maw into a black abyss. This maw is magically linked to your gullet, and whatever the maw swallows, you swallow. Whenever anything touches the magic maw, you may roll a devour attack as a reaction, and may use your actions to start or continue ongoing devour tests for anything touching the magic maw as if you were adjacent to the creature yourself. When a creature becomes fully {@condition swallowed|LustVore}, they slide through the magic maw and down your throat, regardless of distance.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the diameter improves by 5 feet for every two levels above 2nd.

spell.name: Frog's Tongue
entries: Your tongue flies out like a whip, entangling and dragging a creature towards you. Choose a creature you can see within range. They must make a Strength saving throw or be pulled up to 60 feet towards the spellcaster. If the creature is moved within 5 feet of you, they become {@condition grappled} and you may immediately make a {@action Devour|LustVore} attack as part of the same spell cast.

spell.name: Genderbend
entries: You are able to change the sex of any {@condition willing|LustVore} target. Upon casting, declare what sex you wish them to be {@i (female, intersex, male, etc.)}. Their body changes quickly in a flash of magic light. They will appear almost like an identical twin, save with slightly different body structure {@i (or very little difference, if change is only contained to genitalia)}.

When they next take a long rest, or after 24 hours, the spell reverts them back into their original gender. This spell can become permanent if the caster provides 100 gp, which the spell consumes, and takes at least 10 minutes to cast.

spell.name: Greater Belch
entries: While you are filled with at least one prey of any size, you release a prodigious belch, echoing with enough force to lay waste to your enemies. Creatures inside the cone must make a Constitution saving throw or take {@dice 6d8} points of thunder damage and be knocked {@condition prone}. On a success, they take half as much damage and are not knocked {@condition prone}.

spell.name: Healing Massage
entries: As an action, you channel healing magic through your fingertips (or through your body). While this spell is active, as a bonus action you can massage a creature to restore {@dice 1d6} + your spellcasting modifier hit points. Can only be used during combat (DM decides what counts as combat)

spell.name: Heart of the Dragon
entries: You channel the spirit of draconic magic. While the spell is active, if you or an ally within 30 feet becomes {@condition frightened}, {@condition charmed}, {@condition paralyzed}, or {@condition stunned}, you may use your reaction to have the creature reroll the saving throw. On a pass, the effect immediately ends. You may also use your bonus action to choose an ally to reroll on your turn, and on a pass the effect immediately ends.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the duration improves to 1 hour.

spell.name: Heave

components.m: a piece of rotten or moldy food

entries: Your magic forces a predator to disgorge their prey. When you cast this spell against a target that has prey in its stomach, the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they use their next action to regurgitate one creature, chosen randomly. If the target has not {@condition swallowed|LustVore} any prey, they are instead {@condition poisoned} until the start of your next turn.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Hoard Gullet
entries: You move your hands to your throat, chanting in low murmurs as you trace an imaginary line from your lower jaw down to your abdomen. You gain a magical second stomach, which can be used to transport objects and creatures securely. Dragons often use this spell to transport their treasure hoards safely, but it is equally useful to those who would loot such hoards.

You can safely swallow and transport anything you could normally swallow, including creatures. The capacity of your hoard gullet is 500lbs. or 8 points of capacity. Due to the nature of the magic, this stomach is not capable of digestion.
You can't remove individual items or creatures from your hoard gullet, but as an action, you can expel its entire contents into your square or into your stomach.
At the end of the spell's duration, anything still in your hoard gullet is immediately squished into your main stomach.
This magical gut can only be damaged from the inside. Should it take a single point of damage, the spell instantly collapses, making it inefficient to transport hostile entities.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the limit increases by 500lbs. or 8 points of capacity for every level above the 1st.

spell.name: Homunculi Food
entries: You create a living homunculus clone of yourself that looks very similar but has some marks or inaccurate features that make it easily distinguishable from you. This homunculi has the stats of a {@creature Commoner}, and although it shares similar traits and personality to you, it is not very intelligent and desires to be eaten. It also cannot make attacks or attack rolls.
At the end of the duration, if the homunculi has not been digested, the homunculi disappears.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the number of homunculi created increases by one for each spell slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Inanimate Prison
entries: You touch one creature that is either {@condition willing|LustVore} to be transformed, {@condition defeated|LustVore}, or {@condition unconscious}, and magically transform their body. If they have 1 hit point or more, they may choose to roll a Wisdom saving throw to resist. On a failed save or if they are below 1 hit point, this transformation can turn them into any object from tiny size up to their size. This can be something from a rock, to panties, to a statue recreation of them. The transformed creature retains their sentience and are still aware of their surroundings, to an extent, although they do not have any ability to move, speak, gesture, etc.
If the object is broken or otherwise destroyed, the creature immediately regains its normal form where the object was destroyed.

You may recast Inanimate Prison upon a creature under the effects of inanimate prison. Doing so extends the remaining duration up to the maximum duration of the spell slot used to recast it (cannot be used to expand it past the spell's normal maximum duration).

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the duration increases by 24 hours.
In addition, if the cast using a spell slot of 7th level or higher and using 250 gp, which the spell consumes, the spell becomes permanent.

spell.name: Inhale
entries: Your mouth widens and a gale-force wind draws in nearby prey. On the turn you cast this spell you inhale a vortex of air. All creatures in the cone must make a Strength saving throw or be pulled up to 20 feet towards you, taking {@damage 5d8} bludgeoning damage. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is not moved and takes half damage. All creatures that start their movement inside this gale or move into it are considered to be moving in difficult terrain until the end of their turn. A creature reduced to 0 hit points or lower by this damage is instantly devoured by you.
Until this spell ends, you can use your action on subsequent turns to create another vortex of air.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell with a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for every slot level above 5th.

spell.name: Intensify Hunger
entries: Select a creature. Whenever that creature makes a grapple or devour attack, they may add {@dice 1d6} onto their roll.

spell.name: Intoxicate
entries: You weave seductive magic over a target, making them less resistant to your hungry and lewd advances. The target must succeed on a wisdom saving throw or be Charmed by you for the duration. While {@condition charmed}, the target is sexually infatuated with you, and is {@condition willing|LustVore} to be {@condition swallowed|LustVore} and auto fails all tests made during a devour contest (Including resisting the attack and escape attempts).
The spell ends early if the target takes any damage, including digestion damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you may target one additional creature for every slot level above 3rd.

spell.name: Leeching Insides

m.text: a fungus. which the spell consumes

entries: For the duration of the spell, whenever you inflict digestion damage, you regain hit points equal to half the damage dealt.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level, the duration of this spell becomes 10 minutes. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level, the duration becomes 1 hour.

spell.name: Lewd Grasp
entries: Your magically enhanced fingers race across your opponent's body, sending ripples of pleasure through them! You make a melee spell attack against your target creature. On a success, you deal {@damage 1d8} lewd damage, and your target has disadvantage on the next attack they make.
{@b Cantrip Upgrade.} This damage increases by {@dice 1d8} when you reach 5th level ({@damage 2d8}), 11th level ({@damage 3d8}), and 17th level ({@damage 4d8}).

spell.name: Lick
entries: You attempt to whet your appetite on the taste of a nearby creature. Make a melee spell attack against a creature of your choice within range. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d6} psychic damage, and the next devour attempt you make against the target within one minute is made with advantage.
{@b Cantrip Upgrade.} This damage increases by {@dice 1d6} when you reach 5th level ({@damage 2d6}), 11th level ({@damage 3d6}), and 17th level ({@damage 4d6}).

spell.name: Lover's Luncheon
entries: You touch a single target creature whose attitude is at least friendly towards you or is {@condition charmed} by you. The target rolls a Wisdom saving throw at disadvantage, on a failed save that target becomes {@condition charmed} and is {@condition willing|LustVore} to be {@condition swallowed|LustVore} by you. Whether they are eager or shyly reluctant depends upon their personality. This charm immediately ends if you or your allies take a hostile action (except {@condition devouring|LustVore}) towards them or their allies. Despite the name, the spell can be used on any target, not merely disappointing lovers on the morning after.
Once {@condition swallowed|LustVore}, the spell immediately ends. On a successful save, the target knows you attempted to charm them.

spell.name: Maddening Hunger
entries: You awaken a primal hunger within a creature, driving it to feed on whatever prey is closest. A creature of your choice within range must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be cursed by a ravenous appetite.

If the cursed creature is capable of vore, the cursed creature immediately seeks to sate its appetite. On each of its turns, it must use its action to attempt to {@action Grapple} or {@action Devour|LustVore} the nearest creature. If there are no creatures within reach, it moves towards the closest one that it considers possible prey, taking the safest and fastest route possible and dashing if it doesn't end its movement in range of a creature.

If the cursed creature is not capable of vore, it immediately seeks out the nearest mundane food source (such as rations, berries, alcohol, etc.) and devours as much of it as it can in order to sate its hunger.
On any turn it is not able to take a devour action or grapple action or is unable to consume mundane food, it takes {@damage 3d6} psychic damage as it grapples with hunger pains.

The spell ends early if the target reaches Maximum Capacity. The target can make a Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns it successfully swallows someone or something. On a success, the spell ends.

spell.name: Mass Bellyport
entries: Target a creature you can see within the range of the spell. All creatures within a 30 feet radius of the target (excluding you) must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a fail, they are teleported into your stomach.

spell.name: Maximize/Minimize
entries: You cause a creature or object you can see within range to grow much larger or smaller for the duration. Choose either a creature or an object that is neither worn nor carried. If the target is unwilling, it can make a Constitution saving throw. On a success, the spell has no effect. If the target is a creature, everything it is wearing and carrying changes size with it. Any item dropped by an affected creature returns to normal size at once.

{@i {@b Maximize}}. The target's size quadruples in all dimensions, and its weight is multiplied by sixteen. This growth increases its size by two categories - from Medium to Huge, for example. If there isn't enough room for the target to adjust to its new size, the creature or object attains the maximum possible size in the space available. Until the spell ends, the target also has advantage on Strength Checks and Strength saving throws. The target's weapons also grow to match its new size. While these weapons are enlarged, the target's attacks with them deals {@damage 2d6} extra damage.

{@i {@b Minimize.}} The target's size is quartered in all dimensions, and its weight is reduced to one-sixteenth of normal. This reduction decreases its size by one category - from Medium to Tiny, for example. Until the spell ends, the target also has disadvantage on Strength Checks and Strength saving throws. The target's weapons also shrink to match its new size. While these weapons are reduced, the target's attacks with them deal {@damage 2d6} less damage (this can't reduce the damage below 1).

spell.name: Meal of the Phoenix
entries: You imbue reviving magic upon the creature, allowing them to be restored after death. If the creature is digested in the next 24 hours, they will be reborn upon the end of the next long rest or the next dawn in the place of their death (aka inside the creature they were just digested by), whichever comes first. If this is not possible for whatever reason, they will be reborn as close as possible to the place of their digestion.
This spell does not work for any other type of death.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the effects switch to being short rest instead of long rest.

spell.name: Medicinal Acids

components.m: medicinal herbs or a healing potion

entries: You touch a predator, granting them the ability to excrete healing fluids. The predator and each creature in the predator's stomach gain {@dice 1d6} + your Spellcasting modifier of hit points restored per round while the spell is in effect.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the duration of this spell increases by 1 minute per slot level above 3rd. Can only be used during combat (unless by special DM permission).

spell.name: Meltha's Hidden Belly
entries: You reach out and touch a belly, causing onlookers to no longer notice it. Unlike other illusion spells that camouflage one's bulging gut, this simply convinces onlookers' minds that the bulging gut does not exist at all and seems completely normal. Onlookers do not register the fact of the huge gut unless they are actively looking for it. In which case, they may instantly roll to spot past the disguise with advantage.

However, anytime something suspicious happens {@i (such as unusually loud muffled screams, unnaturally loud churning and gurgling, or them accidentally bumping into the gut)}, an observer may roll a Wisdom saving throw against your Spell save DC, gaining advantage if the predator has greater than capacity in their gut. Success means they notice it and may respond appropriately to it. Failure means they make some mental excuse and chalk it up to some natural other disturbance {@i (ex. Loud gurgling could be their own hungry gut, muffled screaming could be a problematic poltergeist, or they might mistake bumping into the gut as bumping into their side or into a chair accidentally)}.

spell.name: Ooze Form
entries: You transform a {@condition willing|LustVore} creature you touch, along with everything it's wearing and carrying, into a slime-like form for the duration. The spell ends if the creature drops to 0 hit points. An ooze isn't affected.
While in this form, the target can occupy the same space as another creature, and move through spaces as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.

Additionally, the target's unarmed attacks deal an additional {@damage 1d6} acid damage. If another creature ends its turn in the same square as the target, they must make a Strength({@skill Athletics}) check contested by the target's Strength({@skill Athletics}) check. The target has advantage on this check. On a failure, they take {@damage 3d6} acid damage.
While in this form, the target can't talk, and any objects it was carrying or holding can't be dropped, used, or otherwise interacted with. The target can't cast spells while in this form.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell with a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the duration increases by 1 hour for every spell level above 3rd.

spell.name: Orgasmic Vibrations
entries: A grand, shuddering orgasm overwhelms your target, sending a constant pleasurable aftershock that makes {@status concentration||concentrating} on tasks difficult. Your target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a fail the creature takes {@damage 6d6} lewd damage and is distracted for the duration of the spell. A target that makes its saving throw suffers half as much and is not distracted.

For the duration of the spell, attempting to cast spells or {@status concentration||concentrating} on spells during the duration of orgasmic vibrations requires a {@status concentration} check equal to your Spell save DC. If doing a {@status concentration} spell, they must roll the {@status concentration} check at the start of their turn. Using skills requiring patience and {@status concentration} requires a {@status concentration} check as well.

spell.name: Perfect Form
entries: You enhance your form to that of a demi-god, becoming a near perfect being. During this time, you are irresistible in every way. Your words are honey, your body is that of a god (or goddess), your scent is heaven and your taste is euphoria.  Your body is enhanced and often gains some divine-like qualities, such as sprouting wings, a heavenly glow (or demonic glow), horns/halo/tail, etc.

All creatures within 120 feet who can see you, touch you, smell you, taste you, or feel you must roll a Wisdom saving throw when you first cast this spell, and at the end of any turn they fulfill one of those conditions. On a fail, they are {@condition charmed} by you, and remain {@condition charmed} as long as this spell continues. They regard you as someone to be worshipped and loved, and will fulfill any non-suicidal demands or requests you make of them. If you or your allies damage the {@condition charmed} creature, it may reroll the saving throw to break the charm. Otherwise, creatures affected by this charm cannot break the charm under normal conditions, although some magical effects or other abilities (such as a Paladin's Aura) may break it.

spell.name: Power Word Consume
entries: You utter a word of power that teleports one creature within range to be teleported into your guts. If the creature you choose has 100 hit points or fewer, it is instantly teleported into your stomach. Otherwise, the spell has no effect.

spell.name: Power Word Orgasm
entries: You touch a creature and speak a word of power that overwhelms a creatures body and mind, causing them to instantly experience a mind-breaking orgasm that paralyzes their body. If the target is below 100 hit points, the target is {@condition paralyzed}. Otherwise, the spell has no effect.
The {@condition paralyzed} target must make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, this stunning effect ends.

spell.name: Promise of Pleasure
entries: You touch a creature to send a ripple of pleasure down its spine as you whisper the dirty things you'll do to them in its ear.

They must make a Wisdom saving throw or take {@damage 4d8} lewd damage and be {@condition charmed}, and half as much damage and not {@condition charmed} on a pass. During this time they are tempted by your eroticism and are sexually attracted to you, and do not regard lewd damage or lewd attacks as hostile. The spell lasts for the duration or until you or your allies do anything hostile towards it, such as {@condition devouring|LustVore} or dealing non-lewd damage.
Since the target creature does not regard lewd damage and attacks as hostile, they are able to do lewd strikes and other lewd abilities/attacks towards you.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each slot level above 3rd.

spell.name: Psychic Touch
entries: As an action, you can cast psychic touch on one creature within 30 feet. While psychic touch's duration is ongoing, you can manipulate the target's smell, touch, and taste sensations at will. Some examples of this include:

items: A sensual {@condition invisible} finger grazing along their thighs.
A heavenly aroma that blocks out everything else.
Making their taste buds believe the bland soup they're eating is rich and delicious.

entries: You can only alter one sense at a time, and these effects cannot deal damage. Creative uses of Psychic Touch may provide advantage to interactions, or disadvantage to the targets.
